title: Tech Connectivity

tables.caption: Recommended: Japan eSIM (install before departure)
rows: Easy QR; top up in app

tables.caption: Essential Apps
rows: Camera menu mode; download Japanese offline
IC card on phone — see below
Optional; many shops — often need Japanese phone; skip unless local friend
FX check; low-fee ATM if needed

tables.caption: Suica / PASMO / IC Card
rows: Add Suica to Apple Wallet (or buy physical at station machine)
Tokyo Metro, JR locals, buses, konbini, some vending
Jul 29–Aug 5 — pass for Shinkansen/Hida; IC for local buses/subways
Balance refund at JR East service center before departure (small fee)

tables.caption: Power & Plugs
rows: Type A — same as US flat pins
20,000 mAh carry-on for long train/hike days

tables.caption: Digital Security (Solo)
rows: Prefer eSIM LTE; hotel WiFi OK for backups
Keep US number active for SMS codes
iCloud/Google Drive copies of passport, JR Pass voucher, insurance
Notify bank of Japan dates; use Wise/Charles Schwab-style ATM if withdrawing

bullets.heading: Connectivity Strategy
items: Sakura Mobile / Japan Wireless pocket WiFi — overkill solo; skip unless no eSIM phone.
Airport SIM (NRT/HND): Bic Camera or vending — ¥3,000–5,000 for 10 GB if eSIM fails.

bullets.heading: Pre-Departure Checklist
items: [ ] eSIM purchased + tested at home (airplane mode off, data on eSIM)
[ ] Suica added to Wallet OR plan to buy at airport station
[ ] Google Translate Japanese offline pack
[ ] Offline map packs: Tokyo, Takayama, Kyoto, Osaka
[ ] Visit Japan Web registration complete
[ ] JR Pass voucher / digital exchange instructions saved offline
[ ] Hotel addresses in Japanese in Notes app (one per hub)
[ ] Airline app + KIX departure saved
